name: QuickSigner
summary: Legally binding e-signatures with unlimited documents and no per-envelope caps: send a secure link and recipients sign from any device without creating an account. ISO/IEC 27001-certified, AATL signatures, valid across the US, UK and EU; a fair-priced DocuSign alternative.
best_for: cost-conscious teams that want certified e-signing (ISO 27001, AATL) with unlimited documents from ~$5/mo and a real free tier
skip_if: you need advanced workflow features and integrations of the big suites: this wins on price, not on integration depth
honest_knock: The price is the argument, and the legal ceiling is the limit. QuickSigner's own llms.txt says it issues Advanced, not Qualified, Electronic Signatures, and names its weaker fit plainly: organisations needing QES, contract lifecycle management with redlining and analytics, or on-premise deployment. Below that line it does what it says for a fraction of per-envelope pricing: recipients sign from a link with no account, app or token. A few users report occasional email-deliverability hiccups, which weighs more here than usual because the emailed link is the whole signing route.

pricing.entry_price_terms: per user a month ($48/yr), unlimited documents
pricing.notes: (re-verified 2026-08-17, re-read 2026-09-27 and 2026-10-20, and read again on 2026-11-13 on QuickSigner's redesigned pricing page) Free, shown as 'Personal Plan (free)' inside the app: 5 documents a month, 3 signers and 1 document per request, PDF up to 5 MB, signature and stamp fields, certificate and diploma sealing, and uploads from Google Drive. Business is $5 per user a month ($48 a year, so $4 a month billed yearly) and is where documents become unlimited: 10 signers and 3 documents per request, PDF or Word up to 10 MB, 10 reusable templates, signing order, reminders, a saved signature, and search, filters, tags and reports. Professional is $15 per user a month ($144 a year): 50 signers and 10 documents per request, 15 MB, unlimited templates, OTP verification by SMS or WhatsApp, editing a request after sending, bulk send, teams, priority support and the eSignature API. Enterprise is priced on a custom quote for high API volume, custom approval flows and large teams. Annual billing saves 20%, and Business and Professional carry a 14-day free trial. The API has a free developer account with unlimited test requests; going live requires Professional, which includes the first 50 production sign requests free, then $0.30 per request, with a lower rate above 500 requests a month. llms.txt adds that completed test documents are watermarked. ISO/IEC 27001:2022-certified and AATL, legally binding under the ESIGN Act, UETA and eIDAS.

sessions.what: Tested by our team on 5 November 2026 on the free Personal plan: Daan created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in Daan's browser. We read the plan page, uploaded one fictional PDF into a new sign request and stopped there. We added no signer, sent nothing and signed nothing.
findings: After sign-up the app opens on an empty 'Sent documents' list with 'Personal Plan (free)' in the sidebar. No card, no sales call and no linked account.

My Account lists Business at 5.00 USD a month or 48.00 USD a year, and Pro at 15.00 USD a month or 144.00 USD a year, all marked with a 14-day trial period. The Business and Pro amounts match our own price rule from 20 October. Checkout, tax and seats are untested.
Templates are 'Available only with a Business plan'.

In a new sign request we uploaded our PDF 'attachment-AIBM-001.pdf'. The app shows it as 'attachment_AIBM_001.pdf', with underscores for hyphens. This is how the upload is displayed, not an export or a content comparison.
Without a signer the form says 'You must fill in at least one signer' and the Send button stays grey.
not_tested: Sending, signing, downloading a signed file and the audit trail: no signer was added
The second kit PDF; we uploaded one
Checkout, tax, seats and the final price
Support, roles, API access, invitations and downgrade; the plan is free, and the account page also offers account deletion, which we left to the account holder
